Question B-006-005-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Line loss attenuates the reflected wave as it travels from the antenna back to the station. Because the returning wave has made the extra trip through the lossy line, the station-end meter sees a smaller reflected-to-forward ratio and a lower apparent SWR.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It decreases the SWR, because less power reaches the antenna": Less forward power reaching the antenna is only the loss itself; the SWR reading decreases because the reflected wave is also attenuated on the return path before it reaches the meter.
- sourceIndex 2: "It has no effect, because SWR compares voltages": SWR compares voltages at the place where it is measured, and attenuation changes the forward/reflected voltage ratio seen at the station.
- sourceIndex 3: "It has no effect, because forward and reflected power are both affected": Forward and reflected waves are not affected symmetrically at the station meter: the reflected wave has travelled to the antenna and back, so it has suffered additional attenuation.
